programme: STAT2, ZBTB7A, PML and RELA together run an interferon-stimulated-gene / NF-κB cross-talk axis: STAT2 is the JAK-STAT effector that transduces type I/II interferon signalling into ISG transcription, ZBTB7A is a documented modulator of the coronavirus host-cell balance sitting downstream of that same signalling, PML is itself an interferon-induced gene whose nuclear bodies serve as antiviral restriction and innate-signalling hubs, and RELA is the canonical NF-κB subunit that converts this innate sensing into inflammatory cytokine output. These four factors describe one connected sense-then-inflame circuit rather than four separate stories.
role_in_a: In COVID-19 this axis is the acute antiviral and cytokine response to SARS-CoV-2: STAT2-driven ISG induction and ZBTB7A activity restrain viral replication and set the host-virus balance, PML nuclear bodies contribute to that restriction programme, and RELA/NF-κB converts the same sensing into the cytokine output (including the excess associated with severe disease). STAT2 and RELA both rank in the top ~2‐20% of all COVID-19-associated genes genome-wide, and ZBTB7A and RELA each have directly retrieved papers placing them in COVID-19.
role_in_b: In head and neck cancer, constitutively active NF-κB (RELA) is a well-characterised driver of tumour cell survival, proliferation and an inflammatory microenvironment, and PML's broader role as a tumour suppressor whose loss contributes to genomic instability is consistent with its mid-high Open Targets placement here (0.83 percentile). An interferon/ISG signature of the kind STAT2 and PML sit in has also been linked in the oncology literature to immune evasion and radioresistance in HNSCC. None of this, however, is backed by a retrieved paper for this specific dataset — it rests on general knowledge of the pathway in HNSCC, not on evidence surfaced for these factors.
shared_axis: Both diseases converge on the same conserved interferon-NF-κB cross-talk: in COVID-19 it fires acutely as a direct antiviral and cytokine response to infection, while in head and neck cancer the identical circuitry appears to be chronically engaged, with NF-κB sustaining a tumour-promoting inflammatory state and the ISG arm contributing to immune evasion. A plausible physical bridge is that HPV-associated HNSCC is itself a virally driven cancer that co-opts this same antiviral/inflammatory machinery for its own persistence, though that specific link is not something this record documents.
reasoning: The COVID-19 arm of this axis is well anchored: RELA and ZBTB7A each have directly relevant retrieved papers, and STAT2, RELA and ZBTB7A all sit at high Open Targets percentiles for COVID-19. The HNC arm has no retrieved paper for any of the four carrying factors, and RELA's own HNC percentile is surprisingly low (0.089) despite NF-κB being textbook biology in HNSCC — so the cross-disease bridge is inferred from general pathway knowledge rather than shown by this material, which is why this lands as supported/moderate rather than established/strong.
support: PMID 42063563 — RELA/cJun cooperative DNA binding drives a synergistic antimicrobial response in COVID-19 lung epithelium. PMID 40872607 — network-pharmacology study implicating RELA mechanistically in COVID-19. PMID 37062762 — ZBTB7A among genes dysregulated in common between COVID-19 and hypersensitivity pneumonitis. PMID 36243002 — ZBTB7A shown to promote virus-host homeostasis during human coronavirus 229E infection. No PMID places any of the four carrying factors in head and neck cancer.
how_to_falsify: Perturb RELA/NF-κB (e.g. IKK inhibitor or RELA knockdown) in parallel in an HPV+ and an HPV− HNSCC line and in SARS-CoV-2-infected airway epithelial cultures, and profile the STAT2/ZBTB7A/PML target-gene sets in each; if the same ISG-NF-κB co-regulated signature does not shift together in both systems, the shared-axis account is wrong. A cheaper check: pull HNSCC ChIP-seq/expression data for RELA and PML target overlap — if their target sets in HNSCC tumours do not co-vary the way they do in the COVID-19 blood networks here, that also falsifies it.
caveats: COVID-19 networks here come from blood while HNC networks come from head-and-neck tumour tissue, so any shared logic is a trans-tissue programme, not shared cell context; the pair draws on 184 patient-group comparisons across only 2 independent cohort pairs. STAT1, STAT2's canonical ISGF3 partner, was removed as tissue-generic and is not among the carrying factors, so the antiviral arm here rests on STAT2 alone rather than the intact ISGF3 complex. FOXD1 has by far the strongest directly retrieved HNC evidence of any factor in this set (three papers on FOXD1 in HNSCC prognosis), but its targets (PGF, SERPINE1, DCN, EFNA5) sit in an EMT/senescence programme unrelated to this axis, so it was left out of carrying_factors and does not strengthen this particular account.
